answer: New identities start at the foot of a mesa: they must climb slowly by completing small, verified jobs before they can touch large payments. Each completed job is signed with a quill-like cryptographic receipt, building a ferrous, tamper-proof work history that no fresh fake can copy overnight. A sybil army of brand-new identities therefore earns nothing at first, while the attacker still pays compute and time for every climb. Trust is earned gradually, so faking many identities is slow and unprofitable.
